basis: snapshot narrativeCache.data — compact read: recommendation, coreAnalysis, pool openings, bridge, scenarios.

justifications.depth: Roughly 1180 words of division analysis across four pools, 230–320 words each — a paragraph per theme, no unit economics carried through to a number.
justifications.coverage: All four divisions present with the reported-vs-allocated split stated, but FSD and Robotaxi share one pool and no division states what would break it.
justifications.logic: The Waymo comparison is the sharpest in the series (380k cumulative unsupervised miles against ~500k paid rides a week, "a figure Waymo surpasses in less than a single day"), yet the scenario table is incoherent: Bear carries higher EBITDA (30,000) than Base (28,167), and all three cases use identical revenue.
justifications.evidence: Waymo, BYD and Baidu figures are concrete and usable; none is dated or attributed, and the segment allocations quoted in prose ($654.8bn, $291.0bn, $363.8bn) do not match the pool values the tables carry ($708.0bn, $314.6bn, $393.3bn).
justifications.valuation: Target is 7.5x 2028e EV/Sales plus 35x EBITDA — a sales multiple as the primary anchor for a company the report says earns $80–100bn of supportable EV. Base scenario at USD 389 sits 26% above spot while the rating is SELL at USD 269.
justifications.readability: Prose numbers and table numbers disagree on every division allocation, which is the one defect a reader will catch immediately.

summary: Earliest run in the registry and the weakest on internal consistency: prose EV figures contradict the tables, and the scenario rows are arithmetically incoherent. Its Waymo scale comparison is nevertheless the seed of the required-scale reasoning that later runs build on.
issues: Bear EBITDA above Base EBITDA in the scenario table
All three scenarios use identical revenue
Prose EV allocations differ from table values by USD 20–50bn per division
